title: 了: completed actions
summary: Lets you say an action has happened or is done, as in 我买了一本书.
explanation:
了 right after a verb shows the action is done: 我买了一本书 'I bought a book.' When the object has a number or description (一本书), 了 goes right after the verb; with a simple object, 了 often goes at the end: 我吃饭了 'I've eaten.'

了 is about completion, not about the past as such. For 'didn't', use 没 + verb and drop 了: 我没去. To ask, add 吗 or 没有: 你吃饭了吗？/ 你吃饭了没有？

examples.en: How many cups of tea did you drink?

mistakes.why: When you say 没 (didn't), drop 了.
Describing a past state doesn't need 了; 昨天 already says when.

why: Correct: verb + 了 + number + object shows it's done.
在 before a verb means 'is doing'; it can't go after 买.
吗 goes at the end of a question.
Correct: 没 + verb, no 了.
With 没, 了 must go.
不来了 means 'he's no longer coming'.
了 goes after the verb or at the end, never before the verb.

exercises.why: 了 goes right after the verb when the object has a number.

why: 不上班了 means 'not going to work any more'.

exercises.en: She went to the bookshop and bought a book.
why: 吗 belongs at the end of a question, not after a verb.
